summary:
SeeYou.Earth is an open-source project I am developing to make astronomical data more accessible and interactive.

Inspired by NASA’s SPHEREx mission, my goal is to create an intuitive platform for exploring the sky, visualizing astronomical observations, and comparing changes over time.

I aim to help users identify and investigate celestial objects, including asteroids, brown dwarfs, and potentially undiscovered planets.

By combining NASA datasets with modern visualization and data-processing technologies, I hope to make space exploration and scientific discovery accessible to everyone, regardless of their background.
details:
Overview

SeeYou.Earth is an open-source astronomy exploration project focused on making space observations easier to access, visualize, and analyze.

The project is inspired by NASA’s SPHEREx mission and its extensive collection of near-infrared observations of the sky.

Concept

SeeYou.Earth explores a simple idea: astronomical data should be accessible not only to professional researchers but also to students, developers, educators, and anyone curious about the universe.

The proposed platform focuses on transforming complex astronomical observations into an interactive and understandable experience.

Main Objectives

The project aims to support several complementary capabilities:

  • Sky Exploration: Explore astronomical observations through an intuitive interface.
  • Data Visualization: Display and interpret astronomical images and related information.
  • Temporal Comparison: Compare observations collected at different times.
  • Object Identification: Explore methods for identifying and tracking celestial objects.
  • Scientific Discovery: Support the investigation of potentially interesting astronomical phenomena.
  • Public Accessibility: Make scientific data easier to understand and explore.

Scientific Approach

The project focuses on publicly available astronomical observations, particularly those associated with NASA’s SPHEREx mission.

By examining observations of the same region of the sky across different periods, the platform aims to help users recognize changes in position, brightness, and other observable characteristics.

Such changes may provide useful information about moving or variable celestial objects.

The project also considers the potential integration of astronomical catalogs and complementary observations to provide additional context.

Technology

SeeYou.Earth is designed around modern web technologies, open-source software, and publicly accessible scientific resources.

Its architecture is intended to support interactive visualization, astronomical data processing, and future extensions.

The specific implementation and technologies will evolve according to the project’s development and scientific requirements.

Innovation and Impact

SeeYou.Earth seeks to combine scientific exploration with an accessible user experience.

Rather than requiring users to navigate complex astronomical archives and specialized research software, the project aims to provide a more approachable environment for exploring space observations.

Its long-term vision is to encourage public participation in astronomy, facilitate learning, and potentially support the identification of celestial objects that deserve further scientific investigation.

SeeYou.Earth is built around a simple ambition: making the universe easier to explore, understand, and discover.
